## Findings
- claim-1: Reiner–Woo–Yong, arXiv:0809.2981v2, state that the outside-box Schur classes form an ideal \(I_{r,n-r}\), induce \(\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\cong H^\star(G/P_J,\mathbb Z)\), and that \(\{s_\lambda:\lambda\subseteq(n-r)^r\}\) is a \(\mathbb Z\)-basis. [source-2@L1320-L1330|claim=formal-document]
- claim-2: For a bigrassmannian \(v_{r,s,t,n}\) with \(i=s-t+1\), \(j=r-t+1\), Bruhat comparison among \(r\)-Grassmannian permutations is partition inclusion; consequently \(J_v\) is generated as an ideal of \(\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\) by \(\{s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(n-r)^r\}\). [source-2@L1354-L1375|claim=formal-document]
- claim-3: Theorem 5.4 is integral: for a type-\(A_{n-1}\) bigrassmannian with \(\mathfrak S_v=s_{i^j}\), it gives two ideal-generating families in \(H^\star(G/P_J,\mathbb Z)\cong\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\), where \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\) and \(b=\min(i,j)\). [source-2@L1380-L1401|claim=formal-document]
- claim-4: The source retains the project’s trajectory: minimality of both Theorem 5.4 families is explicitly conjectural, while the stronger assertion \(J_v/\Lambda_+J_v\cong\mathbb Z^{\binom{a+b}{a}}\) is stated only as suspected. [source-2@L1495-L1502|claim=formal-document] [source-2@L1517-L1552|claim=formal-document]
- claim-5: The retrieved external-provider candidates contain no exact theorem text relevant to Grassmannian box quotients or integral Schur spans; the arXiv candidates identified concern path integrals or trajectory-data mining, not Schubert calculus. [arxiv:2112.15391v3; arxiv:2403.14151v2]
- claim-6: The supplied primary-source locator proves ideal generation by the containing-box Schur classes, but does not itself explicitly state the stronger equality \(J_v=\bigoplus_{i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(n-r)^r}\mathbb Zs_\mu\). Establishing that equality still requires an integral multiplication-closure argument (for example via Littlewood–Richardson multiplication).
## Strategy
Audit supplied external evidence only. Source-2 grounds the integral box-Schur quotient and ideal generators, but no supplied locator states the complete-intersection presentation
\[
\Lambda/I_{r,q}\cong\mathbb Z[h_1,\ldots,h_q]/(e_{r+1},\ldots,e_{r+q})
\]
or the direct Schur-span equality for \(J_v\).

Bounded negative result: no additional citable theorem with exact statement locator was available in the supplied material. This is not a claim about the external literature generally.

## Gaps
- The polynomial/complete-intersection box presentation remains externally ungrounded.
- The reduction
\[
J_v=\bigoplus_{i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq q^r}\mathbb Zs_\mu
\]
still needs integral Pieri plus generation of the box quotient by the \(h_k\).
- Accordingly, the accepted \(b=1\) and conjectural \(a=1,b=2\) arguments remain conditional on those standard facts.

## Next
Obtain a source excerpt with theorem/proposition locators explicitly giving the integral Grassmannian cohomology presentation and integral Schubert/Pieri multiplication. Then compare its hypotheses (\(r,q\ge1\), ordinary integral cohomology, finite Grassmannian) to \(A=\Lambda/I_{r,q}\), and derive the Schur-span equality by multiplication closure.
